malia-m-cohen.text: Says "Californians deserve to know where their money is going"; sped delivery of the state's Annual Comprehensive Financial Report from years to two months.

source.title: A look at the top candidates vying to be California's controller (CalMatters)

malia-m-cohen.text: Urged "restraint" in state spending during budget negotiations, saying higher-than-expected costs reinforce the need.

source.title: A look at the top candidates vying to be California's controller (CalMatters)

malia-m-cohen.text: Focusing on modernizing FI$Cal and state payment systems rather than duplicating state auditor reviews of agencies.

source.title: A look at the top candidates vying to be California's controller (CalMatters)

malia-m-cohen.text: Endorsed by the California Democratic Party, California Labor Federation and Equality California.

herb-w-morgan.text: Says California "has never conducted a full, top-to-bottom audit of its social services system" and commits to "real audits, not excuses."
Proposes blockchain-backed ledgers and a database of state-funded nonprofit transactions monitored with AI to flag suspicious purchases.

source.title: A look at the top candidates vying to be California's controller (CalMatters)

herb-w-morgan.text: Would "carefully scrutinize the state's spending on homelessness" if elected.

source.title: A look at the top candidates vying to be California's controller (CalMatters)

herb-w-morgan.text: Argues California "spends more than any state in the nation—and still can't explain where the money goes."
Endorsed by the California Republican Party and California Republican Assembly.

notes: Office is largely fiscal administration; little evidence on social-policy dimensions for either candidate.
